title: Yuri Gagarin's birth chart
metaDescription: Yuri Gagarin's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.1° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mercury and Neptune sit 0.6° from an exact opposition — near enough that the tradition reads thinking and imagination as a single working part. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Pisces, but precisely: 18.1°, second decan, 10°–20°, under the Moon in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 11.4° Pisces, Venus at 10.4° Aquarius, Mars at 26.1° Pisces. Mercury in a water sign reads as a mind that absorbs before it argues; Venus in an air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a water sign reads as drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Jupiter and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a trine, 0.4° wide. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, Mercury opposition Neptune at 0.6°, and Jupiter square Pluto at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Uranus while both square Pluto. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. Venus stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Pisces at 11.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Aquarius at 22.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 water, 3 air, 1 fire, 1 earth; by modality, 4 mutable, 3 cardinal, 2 fixed. Mercury, Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.2° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
